instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Record My Contribution
cards.instruction: Get your contribution formally recognized, recorded, or repeated where it cannot be quietly forgotten.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put 'roof repaired by Pat' in the village minutes. I'll hear the next item once you've read that back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We all know you fixed it. Can we move on?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the minutes know it too. They weren't up the ladder with me; give them the name.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We'll thank you at the party. Is that enough recognition?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For the party, yes. Add 'thanks pending' after the roof line. You may close the item once both are read back; then nobody has to remember what we're meant to remember.

beats.text: Leave that certificate out of the frame. My name goes under 'cake design' before I give it the final look.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone knows you designed it. Can't I seal it now?

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Choose the Precedent
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which rule, custom, or prior decision will govern what happens now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The handbook closes this hall at six; the festival permit says eight. Tell me which governs before I let you open tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we keep the front open and lock the back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may, if that's your ruling: permit for public access, handbook for everything else. Is it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. That means the kitchen closes at six, though the supper is at seven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose which ruling I give the cooks: cancel supper under the handbook, or keep the kitchen open under the permit. I'm not sending them two instructions and calling that one decision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who gets the head seat, Grandma or the birthday child? Choose which tradition we're using before I lay the places.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put two chairs there. Would that do?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For sitting, yes. Now choose which tradition decides whom I serve first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Serve them together. Except there's only one birthday pudding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then decide before I bring it in: elders first or birthdays first? I'll divide the pudding after the wish. Until you've chosen, nobody at those two chairs gets to call me over.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Interpret the Custom
cards.instruction: Ask them to apply an ambiguous custom where the wording is unclear. Treat their interpretation as the real test of loyalty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I leave for my shift, tell me how much lasagne you're saving me. Our family says 'a proper portion'; I'll hear your interpretation before you serve seconds.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It doesn't say how big. Would a corner do?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Show me the corner. I'll decide whether that counts as dinner for someone coming home from work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your brothers are asking for seconds. They want that corner too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then set my plate beside theirs before you answer. You choose what 'proper' means for me; I want to see whether arriving later has made me less your family.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our club supports members 'where possible.' Bring me your interpretation with a pen; this is my appeal against losing the allotment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It could mean wishing you luck. Would that satisfy the custom?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not to my satisfaction. Decide whether your membership reaches as far as a signature, then tell me what those words are worth.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Some members want my name kept off it. I'd be upsetting them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose what 'possible' protects: their comfort or my place here. You may tell them I asked directly. I want your interpretation beside my appeal, not theirs delivered through you.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Withdraw the Objection
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to drop a complaint, challenge, or special request and accept the official process.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Drop the demand to question our delivery driver. The missing-parcel claim goes through this form.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your form requires a photo of the parcel I haven't received.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Use a photo of your empty doorstep. That's the delivery location.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you stand in it holding today's newspaper?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, beside the doormat. Put me under 'supporting evidence,' and leave the driver off your witness list.

cards.title: Lost in the Process
cards.instruction: Hide your role in the problem by distributing blame across steps, policies, and unnamed procedures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle the inquiry into your missing parcel. It appears to have stalled between reception and dispatch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You left it on the bus. Can you just admit that?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may record a handover to transport without a receipt. I'll determine which stage failed once we've heard from everyone involved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Both departments are you. Call the bus company.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I will, as inquiry lead. You're on the call to ask about dispatch, transport and receipt control, in that order. Nobody closes this as one person's mistake before my process review is finished.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring me the birthday invitations. I'll decide how we correct this failure in address verification.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You put our old address as the party venue on every card. Shouldn't you rewrite them?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can start replacement cards while I examine why the archive supplied an outdated location.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're the archive. There's nobody else to examine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I rule this a staffing failure across storage, checking and dispatch. You'll be the second checker. Put one corrected card in front of me; we'll repair the process before anyone writes a personal apology.
